visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A woman with long, straight black hair, wearing a loose beige sweater and a long black pencil skirt, walks through a brightly lit modern clinic hallway. She is seen from behind, holding a patterned black handbag and her smartphone. (2) The camera transitions to a close-up of a silver metallic clinic logo mounted on a textured beige wall, which reads 'DRX'. (3) The woman is then shown standing in a consultation room, holding her phone to her ear with her right hand while carrying her handbag. She has a neutral but focused expression. (4) A female clinic staff member wearing a white face mask and navy blue scrubs sits at a marble-top desk, showing a digital calculator that displays the number '20000'. (5) The screen splits, showing the woman's surprised facial expression on the right as she continues her phone call, while the staff member is visible on the left. (6) A final graphic screen appears with a white background, displaying the clinic's logo, social media QR codes, phone numbers, and two physical addresses in Taipei and New Taipei City.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) Cheerful, upbeat synth-pop BGM with a moderate tempo plays. A female voice speaks in a casual, slightly demanding tone, pretending to call her husband to ask for money. (2) A muffled male voice responds through a simulated phone filter, asking how much she needs. The BGM maintains a steady, playful rhythm. (3) A second female voice, clear and professional, announces the total cost of 20,000. A high-pitched 'ding' SFX punctuates the mention of the number. (4) The first woman's voice immediately shifts to an exaggeratedly loud and high-pitched tone, lying to her husband that it costs 100,000. A sliding cartoon whistle SFX and a comedic 'wah-wah' stinger follow the punchline. (5) The BGM continues into the end graphic, ending with a clean fade-out.

narrative_and_purpose.narrativeStructure: Montage: Hook -> Setup -> Conflict -> Punchline -> CTA
narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: This comedic short uses a relatable 'asking the husband for money' trope to advertise the DRX Dermatology Clinic. By showcasing a humorous lie about the treatment cost, it draws attention to the clinic's services and upscale environment in a fun, non-traditional way.
